properties.description: The resource-specific properties for this resource.

identity.description: The managed service identities assigned to this resource. Omitting the entire identity property from PUT or PATCH preserves all current assignments. When provided, PUT replaces the user-assigned identity set and PATCH merges it; null PATCH dictionary entries remove individual identities. Setting type to None clears all assignments.

location.description: The geo-location where the resource lives

systemData.description: Azure Resource Manager metadata containing createdBy and modifiedBy information.

postgreSqlVersion.description: The PostgreSQL major version used by the HorizonDB cluster. API version 2026-10-01-preview supports versions 17 and 18. For ordinary cluster creation, the version is supplied in the request and is immutable after creation. For point-in-time restore, the service obtains the version from the source backup metadata and the request must omit this property. This API version does not support in-place PostgreSQL major-version upgrades.

creationMode.description: The mode used to create the cluster. When this property is omitted while creating a new cluster, the service records Create. PointInTimeRestore creates a new cluster from an available backup; pointInTimeUtc and creationSourceClusterResourceId are then required, postgreSqlVersion must be omitted because it is obtained from the backup metadata, and creationSourceClusterLocation is required when the source and target cluster locations differ. This property is immutable and is returned as creation provenance. On replacement, omission preserves the recorded value, resubmitting the same value is accepted, and changing it is rejected.

pointInTimeUtc.description: The requested point in time, in UTC. This property is required in every PointInTimeRestore request. For a same-location restore, the service restores the latest backup available at or before this value. For a cross-location restore, the service requires but ignores this value and restores the latest available backup; cross-location responses omit this property. This property must be absent for other creation modes or when creationMode is omitted and can only be specified during resource creation.

creationSourceClusterResourceId.description: The Azure resource ID of the source HorizonDB cluster used by the selected creation mode. This property is required for PointInTimeRestore and other source-based creation modes, and must be absent when creationMode is Create or omitted. A source cluster does not need to have a pool to be restored, provided an available backup exists. This immutable creation-provenance value does not change after creation.

creationSourceClusterLocation.description: The Azure location of the source HorizonDB cluster used for point-in-time restore. This property is optional when the source and target cluster locations are the same. It is required when the source cluster location differs from the target cluster location and must identify the source cluster's location. This property must be absent for creation modes other than PointInTimeRestore or when creationMode is omitted. This immutable creation-provenance value does not change after creation.

network.description: The network configuration for the cluster. When this object is omitted, the service defaults it to publicAccess Disabled.

backup.description: The backup configuration for the cluster.

dataEncryption.description: The data encryption configuration for the cluster. When omitted during initial cluster creation, the service uses SystemManaged encryption. When supplied during initial cluster creation, type is required. For PUT updates of an existing cluster, type may be omitted; if provided, it must match the existing encryption type. The encryption type is selected at cluster creation; switching between SystemManaged and AzureKeyVault after creation is not supported.

aiModelManagement.description: Specifies whether AI Model Management is enabled for the cluster.

provisioningState.description: The provisioning state of the cluster.

readWritePool.description: The pool currently designated to host the cluster's read-write node.

publicAccess.description: Specifies whether public access is enabled for the cluster. The service defaults to Disabled when this property is omitted.

geoRedundancy.description: The geo-redundancy state. Geo-redundant backup is not supported when dataEncryption.type is AzureKeyVault.

retentionDays.description: The number of days that automatic backups are retained. The service defaults to 7 days when this property is omitted.

earliestRestorePointUtc.description: The earliest point in time, in UTC, to which the cluster can currently be restored.

type.description: The type of data encryption used by the cluster. When the data encryption configuration is supplied during initial cluster creation, this property is required. For PUT updates of an existing cluster, this property may be omitted; if provided, it must match the existing encryption type. This value is selected at cluster creation and cannot later be changed from SystemManaged to AzureKeyVault or from AzureKeyVault to SystemManaged.

primaryKeyUri.description: The versionless Azure Key Vault key URI used to encrypt the cluster's primary storage. Key version paths are not supported. During initial cluster creation, this property can be provided together with primaryUserAssignedIdentityId. For updates to an existing cluster through PUT or PATCH, this property and primaryUserAssignedIdentityId cannot both change in the same request; the first update must complete before submitting a separate update for the other property.

primaryUserAssignedIdentityId.description: The Azure resource ID of the user-assigned managed identity used to access the primary encryption key. The identity must also be assigned to the Cluster through its top-level identity property. During initial cluster creation, this property can be provided together with primaryKeyUri. For updates to an existing cluster through PUT or PATCH, this property and primaryKeyUri cannot both change in the same request; the first update must complete before submitting a separate update for the other property.

primaryEncryptionKeyStatus.description: The validation status of the primary encryption key. This property is returned for AzureKeyVault encryption and is absent for SystemManaged encryption.

primaryEncryptionKeyCurrentVersion.description: The current version of the primary encryption key used by the cluster. This property is returned for AzureKeyVault encryption and is absent for SystemManaged encryption.

designatedPoolResourceId.description: The Azure resource ID of the pool designated to host the cluster's read-write node. The pool is a child resource of this cluster. When a pool is created while the cluster currently has no pools, the service automatically sets this property to the new pool's resource ID, including when all pools that existed earlier in the cluster's lifetime were deleted. This property is absent when no pool is designated, such as after clearReadWritePool succeeds.

type.description: The managed identity type assigned to the cluster. Setting this property to None clears all managed identity assignments.

userAssignedIdentities.description: The user-assigned managed identities associated with the cluster. When supplied on PUT, this dictionary replaces the complete set of assignments. When supplied on PATCH, entries are merged with the existing set and a null value removes the corresponding identity. Each dictionary key must be the full Azure resource ID of a Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities resource. Non-null request values can be empty objects; response values contain the service-populated clientId and principalId. Assigning an identity does not grant it access to destination resources; required role assignments must be configured separately.

principalId.description: The principal ID of the assigned identity.

clientId.description: The client ID of the assigned identity.

createdBy.description: The identity that created the resource.

createdByType.description: The type of identity that created the resource.

lastModifiedBy.description: The identity that last modified the resource.

lastModifiedByType.description: The type of identity that last modified the resource.

lastModifiedAt.description: The timestamp of resource last modification (UTC)

computeModel.description: The required compute model for the HorizonDB pool.

nodeCount.description: The required number of nodes to allocate and assign to the pool. Allowed values are 1 through 16. To deallocate runtime compute without changing the configured node count, stop the pool.

highAvailability.description: The required high-availability configuration for the pool. mode must be Disabled when nodeCount is 1, and must be AnyZone or ZoneRedundant when nodeCount is 2 through 16.

parameterGroup.description: The required parameter group associated with the pool. When creating a new pool in this API version, the caller must supply the corresponding default parameter group; customer-created parameter groups are not accepted during creation. For an existing pool, PUT or PATCH can associate either the corresponding default parameter group or a customer-created parameter group. The create-visible shape intentionally supports both resource ID forms so a future API version can allow customer-created parameter groups during creation without a breaking schema change.

scheduledMaintenance.description: The scheduled maintenance configuration for the pool. The properties available depend on the selected maintenance management type.

provisioningState.description: The provisioning state of the pool.

computeProcessor.description: The processor type for the compute model.

computeGeneration.description: The compute generation for the compute model.

vCores.description: The number of vCores. Allowed values are 1 through 192.

mode.description: The high-availability mode. Disabled is required when nodeCount is 1. AnyZone or ZoneRedundant is required when nodeCount is 2 through 16.

parameterGroupResourceId.description: The Azure resource ID of the associated parameter group. Initial pool creation in this API version requires the corresponding Microsoft.HorizonDb/locations/parameterGroups resource. For an existing pool, PUT can specify either the corresponding default group or a customer-created Microsoft.HorizonDb/parameterGroups resource.

applyMethod.description: Determines when dynamic parameter changes from the associated parameter group become effective. Static parameter changes always require a customer-initiated pool Restart, regardless of this value. Stop followed by Start and scheduled maintenance do not apply pending parameter changes.

syncStatus.description: The synchronization status between the pool and its parameter group. PendingReboot changes remain pending across Stop, Start, and scheduled maintenance and become effective only after a customer-initiated Restart.

maintenanceManagementType.description: Specifies whether scheduled maintenance is managed by the system or by the user.

scope.description: The scope of the endpoint. Cluster-scoped Endpoints provide the cluster connection, and Pool-scoped Endpoints provide read-only connections to eligible nodes in one pool.

associatedResourceId.description: The Azure resource ID of the Endpoint's lifecycle owner. For Cluster scope, this identifies the parent Cluster with which the Endpoint is created and deleted. For Pool scope, this identifies the Pool with which the Endpoint is created and deleted; the Pool must be a child of the Endpoint's parent Cluster.

fullyQualifiedDomainName.description: The service-generated fully qualified domain name of the endpoint. A Cluster-scoped Endpoint uses <cluster>.<clusterid>.<region>.horizondb.azure.com. A Pool-scoped Endpoint uses <poolid>.<cluster>.<clusterid>.<region>.horizondb.azure.com.

role.description: The routing role of the endpoint. A Cluster-scoped Endpoint normally has the ReadWrite role. Pool-scoped Endpoints have the ReadOnly role and route only to allocated nodes in the associated Pool that are not currently playing the read-write role. A Pool-scoped ReadOnly Endpoint has no routing destination unless at least one such node exists, including when the Pool is Stopped, has zero allocated nodes, or has only one allocated node and that node is playing the read-write role.
